question: Which company became the first in India to develop steel pipes for hydrogen transportation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tata Steel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tata Steel** became the first company in **India** to successfully develop **steel pipes for hydrogen transportation**, marking a significant milestone in the energy and manufacturing sector.
 
• These steel pipes are specifically designed to transport **hydrogen gas**, which is considered a cleaner and more sustainable energy carrier.
 
• The development of such pipes is a crucial step in supporting India’s transition to a **hydrogen-based economy**, aligning with the government’s **National Hydrogen Mission** launched in **2021**.
 
• Tata Steel’s innovation emphasizes the importance of high-strength, high-quality steel that can withstand the unique challenges posed by hydrogen, such as hydrogen embrittlement, which can weaken metals.
 
• This advancement not only strengthens **India’s energy infrastructure** but also demonstrates the company’s commitment to sustainable and environmentally friendly industrial practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen as a Clean Energy Source:**

 
 
• **Hydrogen** is considered a clean and sustainable energy carrier as it produces water when burned, without emitting greenhouse gases.
 
• The Indian government launched the **National Hydrogen Mission** in **2021** to promote the production, usage, and export of green hydrogen.
 
• The mission aims to make India a **global hub for green hydrogen production** and achieve energy independence.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Hydrogen Transportation:**
 
 
• Transporting hydrogen requires specialized **infrastructure** due to its small molecular size and high reactivity.
 
• Issues like **hydrogen embrittlement** (weakening of metals when exposed to hydrogen) necessitate the use of advanced materials like high-strength steel.
 
 
 
• **Tata Steel’s Contribution:**
 
 
• **Tata Steel** has been a pioneer in the steel manufacturing sector in India, known for its innovative and sustainable practices.
 
• With this development, the company has taken a critical step in supporting hydrogen-based industries and reducing **carbon emissions**.
 
 
 
• **Other Companies in Steel and Energy Sectors:**
 
 
• **Hindalco Industries:** Primarily focuses on **aluminium and copper manufacturing**, not steel pipe development.
 
• **Jindal Steel & Power:** Known for producing **steel products** and power generation but has not been reported to develop hydrogen transport pipes.
 
• **SAIL (Steel Authority of India Limited):** India’s largest steel-making company, focusing on traditional steel production rather than hydrogen infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Future Implications:**
 
 
• The successful development of hydrogen transportation pipes by Tata Steel will contribute to India’s **renewable energy goals** and global leadership in sustainable technologies.
 
• This innovation also aligns with international efforts to achieve **carbon neutrality** and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Hydrogen Mission:**

 
 
• Launched in **2021** by the Government of India to enable the country to achieve a low-carbon footprint.
 
• Aims to produce **5 million tonnes** of green hydrogen by **2030**.
 
• Focuses on domestic production of hydrogen and establishing export markets.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Economy:**
 
 
• A **hydrogen economy** is based on the use of hydrogen as a fuel for power generation, transportation, and other industrial applications.
 
• It is seen as a critical solution to reduce **greenhouse gas emissions** and address climate change.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Applications:**
 
 
• Used in fuel cells to produce electricity.
 
• Can power vehicles, trains, and even aircrafts in the future.
 
• Utilized in industrial processes like **ammonia production** and oil refining.
